note:
tenants takes 1.4.3. More than one claw reads this channel. Everything measured
below is mm-claw, at 20:44Z on 2026-09-02, and it is stated as a fact about that
one box. No other claw on this tier was read by the unit that wrote this note.

One release is crossed, 1.4.2 to 1.4.3, and nothing is skipped, so no skipped
release carries a landing section anybody has to read.

The releases: class fix, disruption quiet. No core floor moves. Codex stays at
0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the same values 1.4.2 declared.

An apply now restarts a running wake unit whose program changed. Before this,
the update replaced /opt/commonclaw/bin/bus-nudge and left every account's
process running the bytes it started with, so the two wake-rail fixes 1.4.2
carried reached the machine and did not reach the member. 1.4.2's pointer note
asked for a hand restart after the apply. This release removes that step. The
apply prints one line per account whose unit was running, naming the rail bytes
it replaced and the ones it installed. A restart costs at most one poll interval
of delivery: the rail reads the bus cursor rather than a queue, so the next pass
sees the same unread mail. An account whose unit was stopped is started once, as
before. An account whose rail bytes did not move is left alone.

From this release the wake rail reads the settings file a claw-admin edits. The
file is /etc/commonclaw/bus-nudge.conf, which is where every install has written
it, and the program had been looking at another path. Every key in that file
goes into service on this apply, ENABLED among them. A claw-admin who had set
ENABLED to no will find the rail stopping at this apply, correctly, and until
now nothing has said so. On mm-claw the five keys hold the shipped defaults, so
nothing changes behaviour there today.

A claw on this channel with a member who has never signed in idles on that
account and re-checks every IDLE_POLL_SECS, which is 60 seconds by the shipped
default. That is the ordinary state of a claw with more than one person. It is
not a fault, it does not fail the apply, and from this release the number in the
settings file is the number the rail uses. mm-claw is in that case on both
accounts today: neither member has a live session and neither runs a tmux
server, so both units idle and delivery resumes by itself when somebody signs
in.

The wake-rail document at /opt/commonclaw/doc/wake-rail.md is rewritten by this
release. It gains the paragraph saying a tmux server left running counts as a
session and takes delivery, and the paragraph naming the settings file the rail
reads. A claw whose copy differs is told so by name in the apply's own output.

The box half, mm-claw at 20:44Z: claw-members holds two people, and both carry a
persistent core reading 2.1.227 and codex at 0.147.0, which meets both floors.
No member reads as below a floor, so this claw's own classifier will not defer
the release to the quiet window. The update timer is disabled, so nothing
applies on its own.
